Occupational profile | Fixed occupation 0437, undertakers and funeral arrangers, corresponds to 39-4031.00, not the combined OOH funeral service statistics. Arrange and direct individual funeral services. All 22 tasks are core: supervise preparation and care of remains; obtain information needed for death certificates/burial permits; embalm as needed; discuss obituaries, caskets and ceremonies with families; collect and transport remains; arrange grave opening and closing; schedule funerals, burials, cremations and wreaths; close caskets and lead processions; explain and display products; comfort families; prepare remains and documents for interstate transport; negotiate prearrangements; keep accounts and order supplies; arrange transport for remains, mourners, pallbearers, clergy and wreaths; officiate religious services; arrange venues, lighting and flowers; clean facilities; recruit, train and supervise staff and operations; explain survivor benefits; explain pallbearer duties; guide seating; and conduct community outreach. Management, business, and embalming roles may be combined. Embalming as needed is not merely assistance; task descriptions confer no authority to determine causes of death or sign certificates.

entries: Preparation and care of remains | Supervision, execution, and embalming | Supervise and carry out preparation and care of the deceased, perform embalming as needed, and collect and transport remains from the place of death.

Families and funeral arrangements | Discussion, scheduling, and coordination | Discuss and arrange funeral details with families, friends, or legally authorized persons. Plan, schedule, and coordinate funerals, burials or cremations, including wreaths, times, and places.

On-site work and processions | Casket closure, direction, and transport | Close caskets and lead funeral processions; plan casket positioning, lighting, and floral displays; arrange transport for remains, mourners, pallbearers, clergy, and wreaths.

Permits and documents | Death certificates and burial permits | Obtain information needed to complete legal documents such as death certificates and burial permits, and prepare documents for preparation and transport of remains for interstate burial.

Products and clients | Services, goods, and prearrangements | Provide funeral service, product, and merchandise information, maintain casket display areas, discuss and negotiate prearranged funerals, and inform survivors about benefits they may qualify for.

Operations and teams | Finance, operations, and community | Maintain financial records, orders, and accounts; manage funeral home operations, including recruiting, training, and supervising embalming, funeral service, and other personnel; and participate in community events.

Mainland China | Funeral regulations revised in 2025 took effect on 2026-03-30. Article 25 reserves remains collection and transport, storage, embalming, cosmetic preparation, and cremation to funeral homes; Article 26 requires a death certificate for collection and transport; Article 28 requires a certificate and confirmation for cremation and at least 90 days of video from key areas. Obvious discrepancies in cause of death must be reported to public security under Article 26. Job titles do not authorize every entity to offer the five services or sign death certificates. The 2025 infectious disease law took effect on 2025-09-01; Article 71 distinguishes sanitary handling and notification for deaths from Class A diseases/anthrax and other infectious diseases, rather than applying one protocol universally. Chinese fees | NDRC Price [2026] No. 108 differentiates basic/nonbasic services and institutional nature. No charges outside the list, without required disclosure, or contrary to policy; clients cannot be restricted from bringing their own urns. Trial price-display rules effective 2026-05-31 require consistency across channels in Articles 4/15, disclosure of each service in packages in Article 5, and funeral home nature, rates, pricing forms, bases, and reductions in Article 16. Under Article 24, when consumption precedes settlement, choices and prices must be confirmed before service and settlement receipts must list items and prices. Articles 28/29 prohibit undisclosed charges and fraud; Article 6 requires written agreement for personalized services. Verify local lists and rates separately; managers cannot price arbitrarily. US FTC | The rule applies to funeral providers that both sell or offer funeral goods and provide the two categories of services, including relevant prearrangement agents; holding a funeral-home license is not the sole test. Provide a take-away GPL during face-to-face discussions of service choices or prices; give accurate price information by telephone, without a universal requirement to mail a GPL. Packages cannot replace required itemized prices. Embalming charges require checking the three categories of conditions involving state law, explicit prior permission, or attempts to contact, rather than declaring all charges prohibited. Federal law does not mandate embalming. Retain price lists for at least one year after last distribution and selected-goods-and-services statements for at least one year after the arrangements conference; check state law separately. Information boundary | PIPL6/13/19 covers minimum necessity, lawful basis, and retention periods. Apply statutory sensitive-information conditions and applicable separate-consent rules under 28/29; names, contact details, family relationships, and grief are not automatically sensitive, though health information may qualify. Article 49 allows close relatives to exercise relevant rights for their own lawful and legitimate interests unless the deceased arranged otherwise during life; check security and access under 51. Under 47, do not directly delete information before statutory retention expires. Verify publication and external-provision procedures separately; do not invent family consent.

Editorial comparison | This occupation emphasizes individual funerals and professional operations; managers institutional operations; attendants specific on-site services; coroners statutory death investigations; medical managers healthcare institutions; social managers social programs; rehabilitation counselors cases. Tasks may overlap or be combined; verify actual jurisdictional and institutional qualifications separately.

Core concept of adjacent roles | Most roles in the same group or nearby aim to provide dignified services during vulnerable moments involving life and health while ensuring compliant organizational operations. They differ in responsibility level and outputs: professional arrangement and direction of individual funerals and remains handling; overall funeral home operations, pricing, and compliance; on-site services and execution support; statutory investigation of causes of death; or healthcare, social-service, or rehabilitation management.

This occupation's core purpose | Working with families' or legally authorized persons' needs and the deceased person's remains, translate an individual funeral into executable arrangements, direction, and records within qualifications, laws, and institutional authority: confirm needs and fees, collect and prepare remains, schedule and coordinate personnel and venues, check permits and disclosure documents, direct the site and procession, and archive records so services are measurable and lawful.

Main subjects and bases of adjacent roles | Funeral home managers focus on institutional operations, pricing, personnel, compliance, and budgets. Funeral attendants follow daily workflows and institutional operating standards. Coroners follow statutory investigation authority and forensic and judicial rules. Medical and health services managers follow clinical and medical laws and institutional policies. Social and community service managers follow social-service policies and program rules. Rehabilitation counselors follow rehabilitation and disability-service standards and case needs.

This occupation's main subjects and bases | Families' or legally authorized persons' needs and consent; preparation, care, collection and transport of remains; arrangement and direction of funerals, burials or cremations; permits, credentials, prices and disclosure documents; and organization of remains, personnel and transport. Work follows local practice licensing and institutional authorization, remains-handling, hygiene protection and funeral-premises requirements, consumer price-disclosure requirements, and personal information protection rules.

Management, business, and embalming roles may be combined. Embalming as needed is not merely assistance; task descriptions confer no authority to determine causes of death or sign certificates.

Attendants emphasize daily workflow execution, on-site services and facility support. Coroners emphasize death-report intake, scene examination, autopsy, cause-of-death determination and document issuance. US preparation | O*NET's new-hire requirements questionnaire reports 73% associate's or two-year degree, 15% high school or equivalent, and 11% bachelor's, not workforce education; the remaining 1% is not invented. Zone3/SVP6 to below 7 is a grouping; one to two years of training within it is not an every-job rule. BLS lists typical associate's education, related experience None, and long-term on-the-job training. OOH says occupational supervised training usually lasts 1 to 3 years; in the combined scope most employers require age 21, two years of higher education, supervised training, and state examinations. Verify specific state qualifications; do not import these into China.

Check hours, standby, weekend and holiday schedules, probation and assessment measures, and cross-region or interstate transport and nighttime callouts.

Verification notes | Interfaces with families or legally authorized persons, on-site teams, remains-handling personnel, cemeteries, clergy, finance, and legal staff determine permit, authorization, and responsibility boundaries and must be clear in advance.

05 Interface authority with families, on-site teams, cemeteries, and authorities | Check authority for family or legally authorized-person communication, fee commitments, and complaints; duties and handovers with embalming and cosmetic staff, attendants and drivers; coordination and confirmation with cemeteries, cremation facilities, clergy and pallbearers; and referral paths for missing permits, infectious remains, external personal-information provision, and family disputes.

Verification notes | Traceability and documentation requirements for remains collection, transport and handling, permits, fees, and complaints determine accountability. Establish version, modification, archiving, and access rules in advance.

Undertakers, remains-handling personnel, and supervisors; families and authorities

Performing or arranging embalming, cosmetic preparation, or cremation without licensing or beyond institutional authority, or assigning unqualified personnel; procedural violations, remains-handling disputes, regulatory action, and family disputes

Mainland China | Funeral regulations revised in 2025 took effect on 2026-03-30. Article 25 reserves remains collection and transport, storage, embalming, cosmetic preparation, and cremation to funeral homes; Article 26 requires a death certificate for collection and transport; Article 28 requires a certificate and confirmation for cremation and at least 90 days of video from key areas. Obvious discrepancies in cause of death must be reported to public security under Article 26. Job titles do not authorize every entity to offer the five services or sign death certificates. The 2025 infectious disease law took effect on 2025-09-01; Article 71 distinguishes sanitary handling and notification for deaths from Class A diseases/anthrax and other infectious diseases, rather than applying one protocol universally.

Undertakers, drivers, and on-site teams; you, families, and other road users

Improper coordination or posture during remains collection, transport, carrying or lifting, and negligence in driving, venue or equipment safety; injury, traffic accidents, obstructed services, and liability disputes

Follow carrying, lifting, driving, and venue safety standards with clear assignments; reduce risks involving fatigue, weather, and night callouts. Stop and report safety hazards or equipment faults immediately; do not work under unsafe conditions
Scenario | Nighttime cross-region remains collection after a driver has completed multiple consecutive callouts, with narrow cemetery access and slippery grounds.
Undertakers, on-site teams, and public health personnel; you, colleagues, and families

Inadequate protective equipment, disinfection, or post-exposure response and improper handling or transport of infectious remains; occupational injury and infection, public health, and compliance risks

Hygiene | Article 71 of the infectious disease law differentiates handling and notification for Class A diseases/anthrax and other deaths. Qualified entities apply effective technical standards. The 18% disease-exposure response does not provide a personal protection algorithm.
Scenario | Staff prepare to collect remains of someone who died from an infectious disease under ordinary procedures despite insufficient protective equipment and unclear transport requirements.

Missing information or unclear signature chains for death registration, burial permits, death certificates, and other legal documents; procedural violations, service obstruction, regulatory action, and family disputes

China's Article 26 requires a death certificate for collection and transport; 28 requires a certificate and confirmation for cremation and at least 90 days of key-area video. O*NET's obtaining required information does not authorize signing death certificates or determining cause of death. Distinguish specific ceremony arrangements from professional handling.
Editorial counterexample | A draft schedule marks collection/cremation approved despite a missing death certificate. Wording improvements cannot turn an unconfirmed status into approval.
Undertakers and pricing and compliance leads; families, consumers, and authorities
Risk | Inaccurate price choices and fee authorization may cause disputes. Verify Chinese and US rules separately; do not copy all FTC conditions into China.

Chinese fees | NDRC Price [2026] No. 108 differentiates basic/nonbasic services and institutional nature. No charges outside the list, without required disclosure, or contrary to policy; clients cannot be restricted from bringing their own urns. Trial price-display rules effective 2026-05-31 require consistency across channels in Articles 4/15, disclosure of each service in packages in Article 5, and funeral home nature, rates, pricing forms, bases, and reductions in Article 16. Under Article 24, when consumption precedes settlement, choices and prices must be confirmed before service and settlement receipts must list items and prices. Articles 28/29 prohibit undisclosed charges and fraud; Article 6 requires written agreement for personalized services. Verify local lists and rates separately; managers cannot price arbitrarily. US FTC | The rule applies to funeral providers that both sell or offer funeral goods and provide the two categories of services, including relevant prearrangement agents; holding a funeral-home license is not the sole test. Provide a take-away GPL during face-to-face discussions of service choices or prices; give accurate price information by telephone, without a universal requirement to mail a GPL. Packages cannot replace required itemized prices. Embalming charges require checking the three categories of conditions involving state law, explicit prior permission, or attempts to contact, rather than declaring all charges prohibited. Federal law does not mandate embalming. Retain price lists for at least one year after last distribution and selected-goods-and-services statements for at least one year after the arrangements conference; check state law separately.

Editorial counterexample | A covered US provider gives only packages without required itemized prices; a Chinese package conceals service content, lacks confirmed choices, or charges outside the list. Do not claim all packages are prohibited.

Management, business, and embalming roles may be combined. Embalming as needed is not merely assistance; task descriptions confer no authority to determine causes of death or sign certificates.

subject.name: Undertakers and funeral arrangers
subject.summary: Occupational profile | Fixed occupation 0437, undertakers and funeral arrangers, corresponds to 39-4031.00, not the combined OOH funeral service statistics. Arrange and direct individual funeral services. All 22 tasks are core: supervise preparation and care of remains; obtain information needed for death certificates/burial permits; embalm as needed; discuss obituaries, caskets and ceremonies with families; collect and transport remains; arrange grave opening and closing; schedule funerals, burials, cremations and wreaths; close caskets and lead processions; explain and display products; comfort families; prepare remains and documents for interstate transport; negotiate prearrangements; keep accounts and order supplies; arrange transport for remains, mourners, pallbearers, clergy and wreaths; officiate religious services; arrange venues, lighting and flowers; clean facilities; recruit, train and supervise staff and operations; explain survivor benefits; explain pallbearer duties; guide seating; and conduct community outreach. Management, business, and embalming roles may be combined. Embalming as needed is not merely assistance; task descriptions confer no authority to determine causes of death or sign certificates.
